assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica opened a new class of crystalline-like porous solids with tunable 2-50 nm pores, extending porosity beyond zeolites. It is a clear, original synthetic concept that spawned a large field of mesostructured oxides, carbons and hybrids, catalysis, adsorption, separations and drug delivery, and it motivated structural characterisation by electron crystallography. Judged from structure-to-function in porous materials, this is the discovery I rank most strongly.
assessment.attribution: Mobil's M41S/MCM-41 work (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) and the earlier, independent FSM-16 route (Inagaki, Kuroda and colleagues) are the core. Ryoo (SBA/KIT and ordered mesoporous carbons) and Zhao (SBA-15) are major later contributors, so the credit is spread; I propose the originators of the concept. I cannot independently verify the exact priority between the Mobil and Japanese groups and the allocation of credit within the Mobil team.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than three decades of independent confirmation, widespread industrial and academic use. Recognition is, if anything, overdue, though the field has partly moved on to MOFs and COFs.
uncertainties: Priority and credit split between the Mobil group, the FSM-16 group and the later SBA/KIT developers (Zhao, Ryoo) is contested.
Industrial impact has been narrower than for zeolites, which a committee may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites as solar absorbers produced an exceptional rise in efficiency in about a decade, driven by materials chemistry: composition tuning, defect tolerance and solution processing. The discovery is original (a molecular-ionic crystal used as a thin-film absorber), has changed photovoltaics research, and links crystal structure directly to function.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite-sensitised cells (2009); Park and Gratzel (2012) and Snaith and Lee (2012) established the solid-state, high-efficiency architecture. I propose Miyasaka, Park and Snaith, but Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have strong claims, so the three-person limit makes attribution genuinely hard.
assessment.maturity: Scientific interpretation is still evolving (ion migration, hysteresis, stability). Commercial maturity is not proven, so recognition may be somewhat early, though the discovery is widely replicated.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved for real-world deployment.
Credit allocation among six credited names; any trio omits someone with a serious claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis, based on reversible terminator chemistry and clustered amplification, transformed biology and medicine and reduced the cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude. The chemical innovation is original and has had an extremely large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman provided the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule concept; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing platform and Mayer's work on clonal amplification are parallel, partly commercial contributions. I propose the two with the clearest chemical-method claim; I cannot verify the full priority picture, including the contributions of others in the Solexa team.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with abundant independent validation and decades of use.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the prize as chemistry versus biology or technology and how credit divides across competing platforms.
Others not credited here (for example the broader Solexa team) may deserve recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers lets structures be determined from nano- and microcrystals with diffraction before damage, enabling time-resolved studies of reactions and dynamics. This is directly connected to my own concerns: structure from tiny crystals that conventional sources cannot handle. The enabling-method impact on structural biology and chemistry is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the method and the first demonstration; Fromme contributed the photosystem I nanocrystal sample work; Schlichting contributed time-resolved applications; Hajdu was central to the diffract-before-destroy concept. Credit is distributed, and I propose the three I regard as decisive, with uncertainty about Hajdu's role and status.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed at multiple XFEL facilities, but access is limited to a few facilities, and many results are still method demonstrations or on a few well-behaved systems. Somewhat early relative to impact.
uncertainties: Breadth of scientific impact beyond a few model systems compared with cryo-EM and 3D ED, which are more accessible.
Choice among four credited names, including Hajdu.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large new family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable surface terminations and compositions and applications in energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis. Structure and composition are clearly determined and the design logic is attractive.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 discovery (Naguib, Barsoum, Gogotsi and collaborators at Drexel) is clearly attributable to the three credited names; this is a compact, relatively clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young (about 15 years). Many applications are still at the laboratory stage, and the family is still expanding, so recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: Whether application impact is sufficient yet.
Stability and reproducibility of surface termination control remain active questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores and active sites (structure-directing agents, new framework topologies, shape-selective catalysis) underpins industrial refining and emissions control and connects structure with function. The impact is large and lasting, and structure determination of new zeolites has been central to the field.
assessment.attribution: Davis, Zones and Corma are plausible principal contributors; Tsapatsis and Yu also have strong claims (nanosheets, germanate and open frameworks). It is hard to identify a single discovery as compared with a broad body of work.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used, but the discovery is cumulative and the committee may feel it lacks a single sharp breakthrough.
uncertainties: Diffuse, incremental body of work rather than a single discovery.
Overlap with the zeolite and framework-material recognition that the committee may regard as already addressed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Noncontact AFM with CO-functionalised tips images the internal bond structure of individual molecules and enables on-surface reaction studies. This is striking and clear structural evidence at the single-molecule level, with a lasting impact on surface chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Gross and Meyer (IBM Zurich) performed the 2009 imaging; Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor that made it practical. Eigler and Ho contributed to related scanning-probe manipulation and spectroscopy, which belongs to a different, earlier body of work. I propose the three tied most directly to the imaging.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many labs, but the method is limited to planar molecules on surfaces under ultrahigh vacuum, which restricts generality.
uncertainties: Breadth of chemical impact relative to the visual impact.
Overlap of credit with earlier scanning-probe work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural determination of nitrogenase, including the FeMo-cofactor and the interstitial carbide, gives atomic-level insight into biological nitrogen fixation, a central question in bioinorganic chemistry. It requires rigorous crystallographic evidence, which I value, and the mechanism connects to ammonia synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Rees and collaborators solved the original structures; Einsle contributed the high-resolution cofactor and carbide assignment; Dean (with Seefeldt and Ribbe) contributed genetics, biochemistry and mechanism. The credit is shared among several groups, so any three-person selection is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism (the E4 state, N2 binding) is still being actively worked out, so the discovery is only partly complete.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction is incompletely settled.
Division of credit among structural and biochemical groups.
